specialRules.name: Not Orcs
specialRules.description: each Goblin taken out of action counts as only half a model when checking whether the warband must take a Rout test.

specialRules.name: Runts
specialRules.description: if the group rolls "The lad's got talent", the would-be Hero is immediately killed by his Orc overlords — remove one model instead of promoting.

henchmenTypes.notes: — and never more Cave Squigs than Goblin Warriors in the warband (not enforced by the app; check when recruiting). No weapons or armour, ever — big gob and brutality.

specialRules.name: Movement
specialRules.description: M is null because Squigs have no fixed Move — they bounce 2D6" each Movement phase, never run, never declare charges (contacting an enemy with the 2D6" move counts as charging for the following combat round).

specialRules.name: Minderz
specialRules.description: each Squig must stay within 6" of a Goblin Warrior — if not at the start of its Movement phase it goes wild, moving 2D6" in a random direction each phase (fighting anything it contacts, friend or foe) for the rest of the game.

specialRules.name: Not Orcs
specialRules.description: counts as half a model for Rout-test thresholds.

henchmenTypes.notes: May never be given weapons or armour (often carries a big club anyway).

specialRules.note: The Troll never rolls for Injury after a battle.

specialRules.name: Always Hungry
specialRules.description: 15 gc upkeep after every game, or sacrifice two Goblin Warriors/Cave Squigs to feed it instead; unpaid, the Troll wanders off (remove it).

specialRules.name: Vomit Attack
specialRules.description: instead of its normal attacks, a single automatic hit at Strength 5 that ignores armour saves.

specialRules: Orcs enjoy fighting and looting more than anything else, and Mordheim offers an aspiring Warboss endless supplies of both — ideally taken off other warbands rather than dug up. Distasteful Company: many Hired Swords refuse to work for Orcs — an Orc Mob may only hire Pit Fighters, Ogre Bodyguards, or Warlocks. Animosity: at the start of the Orc player's turn, roll a D6 for each Orc or Goblin Henchman not in hand-to-hand combat — on a 1 the warrior takes offence; roll again: 1 = "I 'Erd Dat!" (charges/shoots the nearest friendly Orc or Goblin Henchman as per the full Animosity rules), 2-5 = "Wud Yoo Say?" (spends the turn hurling insults, does nothing else), 6 = "I'll Show Yer!" (must move at full speed toward the nearest enemy, in addition to its normal move). See the full Animosity entry in the Rules Reference (Leadership & Psychology). Note the source's Goblin list prices Mad Cap Mushrooms at 25 gc at recruitment (the general rare-trade price is 30 + 3D6 gc).
